name: Bit-level layer

dies_to: any lossy re-encode (JPEG, WebP-lossy, MP3, WhatsApp photo)

notes: The classic LSB layer. Payload lives in the low bit(s) of raw sample values (image pixels, audio samples). Cheapest to encode, first thing every statistical detector attacks.

name: Transform-coefficient layer (DCT / DWT)

canonical_over: quantized DCT coefficients (JPEG) or DWT subbands
survives: JPEG re-quantization if the codec's quantization table matches
moderate cropping / rotation with spread-spectrum variants
dies_to: cross-codec re-encode with a different quantization table

notes: F5, jsteg, OutGuess, JMiPOD all live here. Robust to the JPEG codec's own psychovisual pass but not to arbitrary re-encoding.

name: Character-level layer (Unicode codepoints)

survives: most chat clients that don't NFKC on input
dies_to: terminal glyph canonicalization for zero-width chars

notes: Zero-width, homoglyphs, variation selectors, combining marks, tag block. Every text-steg technique operates at this layer. NFKC is the boss enemy.

name: Container / structural layer

canonical_over: the parsed file structure — chunks, marker segments, objects
survives: byte-identical file transfers (HTTP raw, email attachment, GitHub upload)
parsers that preserve unknown chunks (PNG private chunks, ZIP extra fields)
dies_to: structural sanitizers that only preserve fields their parser consumes
format-normalizing re-encoders that strip unrecognized data

notes: PNG tEXt/private chunks, trailing bytes past IEND/EOI, ZIP extra fields / comments, PDF incremental updates. Polyglot files are the ultimate abuse of this layer.

name: Semantic / surface-form layer

canonical_over: the meaning a reader assigns to the message
survives: any pipeline that preserves the words themselves

notes: Capitalization, word choice, punctuation, whitespace patterns interpreted as bits. Hardest to normalize, hardest to hide reliably. `capitalization` and `mathbold` methods live at this layer.
